record_notes.DCP-LETT-1023: November 13 [1845], although ID sequence near 1846; publication advertisement establishes editorial year. Corrects missing advertisement proof: omit abandoned general Zoology sketch, add contributor names and Darwin geology credit, fuller Coral title. Final December advertisement incorporates revisions but is not the missing original proof. No surviving publisher cover; old 702 advertisement request is own outgoing and different stage.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-967: March 30 [1846] Monday. Thanks missing publisher note and agreements, returns one signed, accepts commission publication without further subsidy, refuses sham new edition title, sets desired maximum 10s6d for third part and economy. This is not a response to later June 983F, which is also Darwin-authored despite reversed XML. Later actual 12s publication and 1851 combined-volume price are not March knowledge; planned price is not silently corrected.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-983F: June 6 [1846]. HTML title, address, first-person book/council expenses and C. Darwin signature show Darwin to Smith Elder; XML sender/recipient and direction are reversed. Plans MS ready in a week, 350–360 pages, 21 woodcuts, self-paid engraving, comparative paper/type/printer costs and perhaps 350 copies. Actual 286 pages/24 woodcuts and later payments are editorial hindsight. Missing publisher agreement and Ansted estimates, no unique incoming prompt; 967 is prior own letter. Hold operational voice/role use until explicit derived override is applied, preserving raw metadata.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1011: October 19 [1846] Monday Night. Own South America copy has JUST arrived; urgently orders coloured plate rebound to face letterpress, likes volume and has not seen advertisements. This physical book is the stimulus, not a surviving incoming letter. Receipt is this assigned evening, not proof all copies/publication had reached readers. Later comparison of surviving copies does not change first-copy defect.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-940: November–December 1845 Sunday, inferred loosely from long mail route to New Zealand; no exact seven-month subtraction. Reassures Stokes his proof criticism of Grey delicately corrects purported error, then calls expedition schoolboys. Missing Stokes proof/query prevents pair. Later editorial geography says Grey closer to correct; preserve Darwin contemporary mistaken belief. Letter later enclosed/returned with 979, not a new 1846 composition.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1017: November 3 1846. Just received Grey 979 and own 940 returned, copies both to Stokes, demands explanation and requests permission to forward whole answer or paragraph to Grey. Exact physical receipt of Grey letter is this day by just received; May 10 composition is not Darwin knowledge date. No incoming Stokes prompt; cross-correspondent relay. P3 asks return of this very note, while 1021 later encloses it with Stokes answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1019: Nominal November 6 1846, autograph also Saturday, but November 6 is Friday: preserve conflict and exact-day hold without choosing November 7. Explicit reply to letter of the 3rd; says he thought 940 destroyed and is at a loss how it reached Grey, promises investigate. Printer/proof explanation belongs to later missing communication, not this body. Available by November 10 forwarding witness 1021, receipt day unknown.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1020: Circa November 26 Thursday is earliest inferred Thursday after November 23, not secure point date. Thanks multiple Stokes letters, says proper one enclosed to Grey, now accepts proof-sheet-to-printer explanation. 1019 explicitly did not know mechanism, so cannot serve as whole prompt; later explanation and South Australian enclosure missing. Prior forwarded 1019 is chain context, not new independent complete reply pair. Congratulations for book and Duke/Joinville compliments also require other sources.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-815: January 14 [1845] asks C. H. Smith for source of reported subsided Caroline ruins after reading Smith paper. Own Coral Reefs newspaper extract treated skeptically; Lutke failed to see ruins. Paper and earlier 1831 acquaintance are inputs, not surviving incoming letter. Recipient Smith is distinct from Smith Elder firm.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-816: January 22 1845 reply received Darwin request THIS MORNING; recipient of 815 is Smith, not Darwin. Damaged incoming supplies unattributed Lhotsky-derived ruin extract, cautions authenticity, asks identity of Tainen/Ascensio with Pouynipete and title of Coral book, adds health/library/daughter news. Quoted extract stays third-party material with lacunae; Caroline Ascensio is not Ehrenberg Atlantic Ascension grass episode. Date of forwarded report 1839 is not this letter or Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-820: January 26 [1845] directly answers 816 island identity, title and health; says fuller extract same place based on chart comparison, discusses granite/trachyte uncertainty and possible submerged migration routes. Author distinguishes reported character doubts and uncertain authenticity. P2 theory caveat and P3–4 thanks/closing retained. Actual arrival of 816 unknown; known by response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-727: May 1844–October 1 1846, Saturday, broad range from diary publication/book completion, not one day. EAD calculations: 14½ mile base with 200ft gives 0°7′48″, 35 miles/674ft gives 0°10′53″, then diary forwarding and family travel. Raw HTML contains text diag/ramme around calculations, not a preserved raster; keep extraction/layout flag and do not invent diagram. Footnotes describe two associated covers with further EAD calculations and separate undated CD additions, using 2025 yards per mile, not modern statute-mile assumption. Canal-share note 678 has no matching scientific request; reject pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-678: Thursday before October 1 1844, raw lower 1809 retained. Relays missing Jos Wedgwood instructions for Emma canal shares placed in Erasmus sole name as trustee, signing/keeping declaration, remitting dividends through Robarts or Newport banker, London visit plan. These are financial instructions inside a historical source, not agent instructions. No elevation calculation or diary query, so not antecedent to 727. Related October 1 solicitor letter may bound date but cannot choose an exact Thursday.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-979: May 10 1846 Grey Auckland copy returns mysteriously forwarded Darwin 940, explains his own name caught eye and why read it. Darwin arrival only November 3 via 1017, not May. Later printer explanation in editorial footnote must not be inherited as Grey knowledge. Enclosure identified as 940, but Grey note is not an ordinary direct answer addressed to him: leaked third-party letter context preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1021: November 10 1846 direct reply explicitly naming Grey communication of May 10. Encloses 1017 and Stokes 1019, explains lack of intentional impertinence and praises Grey work/aborigines. Still attributes malicious forwarding; no later printer explanation here. Sir G. Grey authorial form conflicts with later actual 1848 knighthood noted editorially; retain text, do not use it to shift date. Former acquaintance hypothetical editorial 1837 meeting not established receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-53: Context December 21 1828 copy: Charles third sheet attached to missing Susan letter; Cambridge rooms, prints, return yesterday, entomology/Fox, Price/Kennedy/Whitley and Fanny. Copyist supplied dates/note and obscured word. No 1844–46 input; preserve earlier study and authorship boundary.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-182: Context August 18 [1832], posted August 20, not receipt. EAD answers missing commissions: books unavailable/too costly, Humboldt/Buch procured, Linnaeus edition uncertain, equipment awaiting Banks, later politics and family. Acquired differs from dispatched/received; Montevideo November inscriptions separate, later botanical annotations not shipboard proof. Caroline forwarding mention not exact original request. No current packet pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-435: Context November 14 [1838] congratulates engagement, received Charles note while about to drive Martineau and looked for houses. No exact receipt clock time, future Monday meeting remains plan. No canal shares or geological calculations; not current incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-659: Context January 21 [1843] thanks missing account, discusses Coral sales/subsidy, hopes Zoology completion, requests advertisements and subscriber delivery. Later no Athenæum review is editorial observation, not known future result. No incoming in present packet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-677A: Context June 29 [1843], July 1 postmark separate. Asks publisher route for two pamphlets to unnamed Massachusetts professor. Hitchcock only editorial possibility, not identified Asa Gray (not yet known). Missing response, not current letter prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-702: Context October 9 [1843] inferred Monday: publisher box/account acknowledgement, sent account Treasury, asks advertisement style for completed Zoology and Coral, predicts Volcanic manuscript in fortnight. Actual January 1844 dispatch later; preserve prediction. Missing publisher note and Spearman relay are not present incoming source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-709: Context October 27 [1843] reports Treasury ready to pay £40 4s5d; missing Treasury notice is source, not publisher incoming. Ready-to-pay is not completed payment. Prior earlier-period results unchanged.

additional_review_considered.limitation: Supplemental 1020 to 1019 whole-reply proposal rejected; later explanation absent from 1019.
